text:
PACKET-17 — UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no outside source consulted)

Exposure note: nothing in my context proposed an identification of this text. The scribe himself names
scriptural books in citations (ysa. vii, eph. iii, ioh. xii, osee xi, amos vii, exo. xii, iosue); where a
cited verse was recognisable to me, familiarity with the Latin Bible wording may have coloured how I resolved
individual abraded words inside those quotations. I have tried to put a question mark wherever the letters
alone would not carry the reading. I made no attempt to identify the work or author.
Process note: before starting I ran one directory listing of the three packet folders (file names only);
no other file or source was opened.

=====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
=====================================================================
Observations
- Two sides of one parchment leaf used as a pastedown inside a book cover (image-001 = one side, with ruler;
  image-010 = other side, wooden board visible at right). Text upright in both.
- Two columns per side, c. 50-56 lines per column, small compressed Gothic book hand, heavy abbreviation.
- Side A (image-001): left column complete in width; right column cropped at its right edge by the leather
  turn-in (last 1-4 letters of every line lost). A hole in the left column c. lines 10-11 and a larger hole
  in the right column c. lines 11-17. Lower half of left column abraded.
- Side B (image-010): left column loses 1-3 letters at the start of each line under a paper guard; right
  column is very rubbed from c. line 8 to c. line 45, legible only at top and bottom.
- Red: one enlarged red initial "E" (2 lines high) in side A right column at line 3, with a short red rubric
  on the same line ("In nat..."); red underlining of quoted phrases throughout side A right column and
  occasionally in side A left column; small red paraph/touch marks; one word struck through in red in side B
  right column (penultimate line). A marginal note in a red-outlined box stands in the right margin of side B
  beside c. line 30 of the right column (three short lines).
- No running title visible. No interlinear gloss seen.
Tentative interpretation (not observation)
- Continuous prose that quotes short phrases (underlined in red) and then expounds them, moving phrase by
  phrase with "Seq(uitur)". The red initial + rubric marks the start of a new unit part-way down side A
  right column; the text before it ends with a closing formula. Which side is recto is not determinable
  from the images; side B's content (cross / sign) looks like the same matter as side A left column, so
  side B may precede side A, but that is a guess.

=====================================================================
2. SPANS SELECTED / NOT READ
=====================================================================
Selected: side A left column lines 1-29 and the last 13 lines; side A right column nearly throughout
(opening of new unit at the red initial, then the "Seq." chain); side B left column nearly throughout;
side B right column top 8 lines and bottom 8 lines; the marginal box.
Unread / effectively unreadable at this resolution: side A left column c. lines 31-36 (abraded); side B
right column c. lines 9-45 (rubbed) — only isolated words given. A higher-resolution or raking-light image
of side B right column would be needed.

Conventions: (..) = proposed expansion; word? = uncertain reading; [illegible]; [..] = letters lost at a
physical edge or hole, NOT supplied unless marked "?"; "·" = punctus; xp̄ = the chi-rho nomen sacrum.
Line numbers are counted from the top of the named crop, including a partial top line; they may be off by one.
Overlaps between crops are noted and not repeated.

7. LIMITATIONS
=====================================================================
- Crops are roughly 1100 px wide for a c. 6 cm column: minims (in/ni/m/u) and suspension strokes are often
  not separable, so many readings rest on word shape. Every "?" is real doubt.
- Side A right column: line ends lost under the binding turn-in on every line.
- Side B left column: line beginnings lost under the guard on every line.
- Side B right column middle (c. 35 lines) is essentially unread.
- Side A left column c. 6 lines below the middle are abraded and only partly read.
- Column order within each side is left-then-right (side A left column's last line runs on syntactically
  into the right column's first line: "...ideo exaltatus / est ut omnis qui credit..."). Which side precedes
  is not established.
- Total physical lines given with at least partial text: c. 186 (side A left 45, side A right 52,
  side B left 56, side B right 33 incl. margin). Overlapping crop lines are counted once.
